title: Braised Lamb Shanks
summary: Injected lamb shanks braised in red wine until they fall off the bone, over mashed potatoes.
story: Lamb shanks get the injection treatment too, then a hard sear and a long braise in red wine with rosemary and thyme. They come out falling off the bone over a pile of mashed potatoes, with the sauce doing all the talking.

steps.title: Inject & season
steps.body: Inject the shanks, then season with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Sear
steps.body: Sear hard in a Dutch oven until browned all over. Set aside.

steps.title: Build
steps.body: Cook the veggies in the same pot, add wine and broth, bring to a simmer.

steps.title: Braise
steps.body: Add shanks back, cover, and braise at 325°F for 2.5-3 hours until falling off the bone.

steps.title: Serve
steps.body: Serve over mashed potatoes with the braising sauce spooned over.

proTips: The injection plus the braise means these stay juicy all the way through.
Serve over mashed potatoes and let the sauce do the talking.
Skim the fat off the braising liquid before serving if you like.

title: Grilled Lamb Kebabs
summary: Marinated lamb cubes grilled hot and fast with peppers and onions — the marinade does the injection's job.
story: Small cuts can't take an injection, so these kebab cubes go into an olive oil, lemon, garlic, and rosemary marinade overnight. Threaded with peppers and onion, grilled hot and fast to medium-rare. Don't overcook them.

items: 2.5 lbs lamb leg or shoulder, cut into 1.5-inch cubes

steps.title: Marinate
steps.body: Marinate the lamb cubes 4-8 hours (overnight's best).

steps.title: Skewer
steps.body: Thread onto skewers alternating with peppers and onion.

steps.title: Grill
steps.body: Grill hot — 2-3 minutes per side, medium-rare.

proTips: Small cuts can't take an injection, so the marinade does the work — gets the moisture and flavor deep in.
Soak wooden skewers 30 minutes so they don't burn.

title: Smoked Lamb Ribs with Sticky Glaze
summary: Marinated lamb ribs smoked low with a sticky honey-balsamic glaze brushed on late.
story: Too thin to inject, so these ribs get a garlic-rosemary marinade overnight to stay juicy. Smoked low over oak or cherry, spritzed with apple juice, and finished with a sticky honey-balsamic glaze in the last 30 minutes so it doesn't burn.

items: Apple juice in a spray bottle

steps.title: Marinate
steps.body: Marinate the ribs 4 hours or overnight, then apply the rub.

steps.title: Smoke
steps.body: Smoke at 250°F over oak or cherry, spritzing with apple juice every 45 minutes, 3-4 hours.

steps.title: Glaze
steps.body: Brush with the honey-balsamic glaze in the last 30 minutes.

steps.title: Check
steps.body: Pull when they bend and the meat pulls back from the bone.

proTips: Too thin to inject, so the marinade keeps them juicy.
The glaze goes on late so it doesn't burn.
Or use your favorite rub — it's not set in stone.

title: Smoked Cornbread Dressing
summary: Day-old cornbread, water chestnuts for crunch, sage and thyme — smoked in cast iron.
story: Day-old cornbread or it falls apart. Onion, celery, water chestnuts for that crunch that survives the whole cook, sage and thyme, packed into a buttered cast iron skillet and smoked until golden. If you made the jalapeño cheddar cornbread, this dressing gets a nice little kick.

items: 1 can (8 oz) water chestnuts, drained and chopped

steps.title: Sauté
steps.body: Sauté onion and celery in butter until soft.

steps.title: Mix
steps.body: Mix everything in a big bowl — it should be wet but not soupy.

steps.title: Smoke
steps.body: Pack into a buttered cast iron skillet or pan. Smoke at 325°F for 45 minutes until golden on top.

proTips: Day-old cornbread or it falls apart.
The water chestnuts stay crunchy through the whole cook — that's the bite you're looking for.
If you made the jalapeño cheddar cornbread, this dressing gets a nice little kick.

title: Smoked Turkey Gravy
finish: Thick enough to coat a spoon
summary: Made from smoker drippings with just a whisper of rosemary — liquid gold.
story: Save those drippings from the turkey — that's liquid gold. Put a drip pan under the bird and thank yourself later. Whisked into a gravy with just a little rosemary — pull the sprig before serving so nobody gets a mouthful of needles.

items: Turkey drippings (or 4 Tbsp butter + 4 Tbsp flour if you're short)
1/4 cup flour (if not using drippings roux)

steps.title: Roux
steps.body: If you've got drippings from the smoker, whisk flour into them and cook 2 minutes. If no drippings, make a roux with butter and flour first.

steps.title: Whisk
steps.body: Whisk in broth until thick. Toss in the rosemary sprig.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.body: Simmer 10 minutes. Pull the rosemary sprig before serving.

proTips: Save those drippings from the turkey — that's liquid gold.
Put a drip pan under the bird and thank yourself later.
Just a little rosemary — pull the sprig before serving so nobody gets a mouthful of needles.

title: Smoked Mashed Potatoes
summary: Potatoes smoked whole in the skin, mashed with butter, cream, and roasted garlic.
story: Smoking the potatoes whole in the skin keeps them from drying out — and you get a whisper of smoke in every bite. Mashed with butter, warm cream, and garlic roasted right on the smoker. The gravy goes on top of these. That's the whole point.

items: 4 cloves garlic, roasted on the smoker

steps.title: Smoke
steps.body: Smoke the whole potatoes at 275°F for 1.5 hours until tender.

steps.title: Mash
steps.body: Scoop out the insides and mash with butter, sour cream, warm cream, and roasted garlic.

steps.title: Season
steps.body: Salt to taste. Top with chives.

proTips: Smoking them whole in the skin keeps them from drying out.
Warm the cream first — cold cream makes gluey potatoes.
The gravy goes on top of these. That's the whole point.
A little sour cream makes them tangy and rich — Kelly's way.

title: Ember Apple Rub
summary: A sweet Ember rub built on real apple — warm fall spice for pork ribs, shoulder, chops, and chicken.
story: Apple and pork are old friends. This rub puts the orchard right in the jar: freeze-dried apple powder for true apple flavor, brown sugar for the crust, and cinnamon, ginger, and nutmeg for warmth. Use it anywhere you'd reach for a sweet rub — it shines on ribs and pork shoulder.

steps.title: Make the apple powder
steps.body: Buzz a handful of freeze-dried apples in a spice grinder until powder-fine. Measure out 3 tablespoons.

steps.title: Mix
steps.body: Combine everything in a bowl and stir until even. Break up any brown sugar lumps with your fingers.

steps.title: Store
steps.body: Keep in a sealed jar. Use within 6 months for best flavor.

proTips.text: Freeze-dried fruit is in the dried-fruit aisle at most grocery stores — no specialty shop needed.

title: Ember Peach Rub
summary: A sweet Southern-style Ember rub built on real peach — with allspice for that peach-cobbler warmth. Made for pork and chicken.
story: Peach and pork is a Southern love story. This rub gets its peach from real freeze-dried peach powder, backed with brown sugar and a whisper of allspice — the same warmth you taste in a good peach cobbler. Try it on pork chops, ribs, or smoked chicken thighs.

steps.title: Make the peach powder
steps.body: Buzz a handful of freeze-dried peaches in a spice grinder until powder-fine. Measure out 3 tablespoons.

steps.title: Mix
steps.body: Combine everything in a bowl and stir until even. Break up any brown sugar lumps with your fingers.

steps.title: Store
steps.body: Keep in a sealed jar. Use within 6 months for best flavor.

proTips.text: Freeze-dried fruit is in the dried-fruit aisle at most grocery stores — no specialty shop needed.

title: Ember Cherry BBQ Sauce
summary: A sweet-tart Ember sauce built on real dark cherries — glossy, rich, and made for pork, chicken, and smoked meatloaf.
story: Cherries and smoke are a natural pair. This sauce cooks fresh or frozen dark cherries down into a ketchup-based BBQ sauce with brown sugar, molasses, and a butter finish. Blend it smooth or leave it a little chunky — either way it shines on ribs and pulled pork.

items: 2 cups fresh or frozen dark sweet cherries, pitted

steps.title: Break down the cherries
steps.body: Simmer the cherries in a saucepan over medium heat until they soften and break down, about 10 minutes. Mash with a spoon.

steps.title: Build the sauce
steps.body: Stir in everything except the butter. Simmer 15–20 minutes, stirring now and then, until thickened.

steps.title: Blend
steps.body: Blend smooth with an immersion blender — or leave it a little chunky if you like texture.

steps.title: Butter finish
steps.body: Stir in the butter off the heat. Cool and jar. Keeps 2 weeks in the fridge.

title: Ember Cranberry BBQ Sauce
summary: A sweet-tart Ember sauce built on real cranberries with orange zest — thin, glossy, and made for the holidays. Turkey's best friend.
story: Cranberries want to be a BBQ sauce — they're already tart, already red, already built for a glaze. This one gets extra brown sugar to tame the tartness, orange zest for brightness, and a butter finish. Thin enough to brush, bold enough to stand up to smoked turkey and pork.

steps.title: Pop the cranberries
steps.body: Simmer the cranberries in a saucepan over medium heat until they pop and break down, about 10 minutes.

steps.title: Build the sauce
steps.body: Stir in everything except the butter. Simmer 15–20 minutes, stirring now and then, until thickened.

steps.title: Blend
steps.body: Blend smooth with an immersion blender — or leave it a little chunky if you like texture.

steps.title: Butter finish
steps.body: Stir in the butter off the heat. Cool and jar. Keeps 2 weeks in the fridge.

title: Ember Dr Pepper BBQ Sauce
summary: A sweet Ember sauce built on reduced Dr Pepper — dark, glossy, and sticky-sweet. Made for ribs, pulled pork, and wings.
story: Dr Pepper's 23 flavors were practically born for BBQ sauce. This one reduces the soda down to concentrate all that cherry-vanilla-spice character, then builds it into a ketchup-based sauce with extra brown sugar and honey for sweetness and a butter finish. Brush it on ribs in the last 30 minutes and watch it turn to candy.

steps.title: Reduce the Dr Pepper
steps.body: Simmer the Dr Pepper in a saucepan until reduced by half, about 15 minutes. This concentrates the flavor.

steps.title: Build the sauce
steps.body: Stir in everything except the butter. Simmer 15–20 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick and glossy.

steps.title: Butter finish
steps.body: Stir in the butter off the heat. Cool and jar. Keeps 2 weeks in the fridge.

title: Ember Orange BBQ Sauce
summary: A bright Ember sauce built on reduced fresh orange juice with ginger — citrusy, glossy, and made for chicken and pork.
story: Orange BBQ sauce is a real thing — the BBQ Pit Boys did an orange-ginger version, and citrus sauces have a loyal following. This Ember take reduces fresh orange juice to concentrate the flavor, then builds it into a ketchup-based sauce with ginger for warmth and a butter finish. Bright on chicken thighs, beautiful on pork chops.

items: 1 tsp fresh grated ginger (or ½ tsp ground)

steps.title: Reduce the orange juice
steps.body: Simmer the orange juice in a saucepan until reduced by half, about 15 minutes.

steps.title: Build the sauce
steps.body: Stir in everything except the butter. Simmer 15–20 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick and glossy.

steps.title: Butter finish
steps.body: Stir in the butter off the heat. Cool and jar. Keeps 2 weeks in the fridge.
